extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in algebraic topology learning/using Steenrod operations
extracted.subtask_description: Construction, basic properties, and relations (Adem relations, Cartan formula, normalization) for Steenrod squares (p=2) and Steenrod powers (odd p), including the proof that admissible monomials form a basis of the Steenrod algebra and the normalization/definition of P_i.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissible monomials form a basis for A_p
rubrics_metrics.description: The admissible monomials in A_p are linearly independent and hence form a basis for A_p as a vector space over Z_p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof idea: if a linear combination of admissible monomials were zero, apply it to the class ι^n and choose n larger than the excess of each monomial to contradict freeness of H^*(K(Z_p,n); Z_p). Reference: Steenrod & Epstein 1962 gives a more elementary proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess less than n condition
rubrics_metrics.description: In the theorem about admissible monomials acting on ι_n, only monomials with excess less than n contribute: Sq_I(ι_n) = 0 if e(I) > n; if e(I) = n one reduces to lower-excess monomials (or powers thereof) until obtaining e(J) < n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanation: write i1 = e(I) + i2 + i3 + ... ; if e(I) > n then i1 > |Sq_{i2}Sq_{i3}... (ι_n)| so action is zero. If e(I) = n one repeatedly uses power expressions (or β formulas for odd p) to reduce to monomials with smaller excess.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adem relations provide algorithmic reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the multiplicative structure of the Steenrod algebra is complicated, the Adem relations allow systematic reduction of all products to sums of admissible monomials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Adem relations algorithmically to convert any product of operations into a linear combination of admissible monomials; alternative equivalent relations (see next item) can be easier to remember in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compact Adem-type relation: sum_j Sq_{2n-k+j-1} Sq_{n-j} = 0
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a family of relations among Steenrod squares equivalent to the Adem relations: for fixed n,k one has Σ_j Sq_{2n-k+j-1} Sq_{n-j} = 0. When k=0 this is Sq_{2n-1}Sq_n = 0, and other cases come from Pascal's triangle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: expanding Sq_7 Sq_4 yields a table of relations; many entries reduce further (e.g. instances of Sq_{2n-1}Sq_n = 0). Similar relations for Steenrod powers P appear from P_{p n - k + j - 1} P_{n - j} = 0 derived from P_{p n - 1}P_n = 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stable cohomology operations are generated by the Steenrod operations
rubrics_metrics.description: All Z_p cohomology operations that are stable (commuting with suspension K(Z_p,n)→K(Z_p,n+1)) are polynomials in the Sq^i when p=2, and polynomials in the P^i and β when p is odd.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 4L.1 and the structure of H^*(K(Z_p,n);Z_p) below dimension 2n imply the Steenrod algebra A_p equals the limit of these stable operations. This identifies A_p with the algebra of stable Z_p operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stability characterization of A_p
rubrics_metrics.description: A_p consists precisely of all Z_p cohomology operations that are stable, i.e., commute with the suspension maps K(Z_p,n)→K(Z_p,n+1) which pull ι_{n+1} back to the suspension of ι_n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument uses that the suspension map induces isomorphisms on π_i for i ≤ 2n and surjection for i=2n+1, so the inverse limit lim← H^*(K(Z_p,n)) identifies with the stable operations and with A_p via the admissible monomial description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of homotopy ι^{⊗p} T ≃ ι^{⊗p} on the p n-skeleton
rubrics_metrics.description: To construct λ(ι) one needs a homotopy between ι^{⊗p} and ι^{⊗p}∘T on the p n-skeleton (where T permutes smash factors), so that this homotopy extends over higher cells.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute the degree of T on (S^n)^{∧p}=S^{pn}: T is product of (p−1)n^2 transpositions giving degree (−1)^{(p−1)n^2}. For odd p this degree is +1, so restriction is homotopic to identity; for p=2 signs are irrelevant in Z_2. Since π_i(K^{pn})=0 for i>pn there are no obstructions to extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of θ_i (and Sq^i) via ∇^*(λ(α)) expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: Given λ(α) ∈ H^{pn}(S^∞×_Zp X^{∧p}), pulling back along the diagonal ∇ : L^∞×X → S^∞×_Zp X^{∧p} gives ∇^*(λ(α)) = Σ_i ω^{(p−1)n−i} ⊗ θ_i(α). For p=2 set Sq^i(α)=θ_i(α).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ω_j generators of H^j(L^∞); for odd p take ω_1 and ω_2=βω_1; θ_i are cohomology operations increasing dimension by i; θ_i = 0 for i < 0. For odd p one shows θ_i=0 unless i = 2k(p−1) or 2k(p−1)+1, and defines P^k from θ_{2k(p−1)}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cartan formula and associated sign in λ
rubrics_metrics.description: λ(α∪β) = (−1)^{p(p−1)mn/2} λ(α) ∪ λ(β) for |α|=m, |β|=n; this yields the Cartan formula for Steenrod operations (with the appropriate signs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For p=2 the sign exponent simplifies and one obtains Sq^i(α∪β)=Σ_j Sq^j(α)∪Sq^{i−j}(β). The sign factor arises from permuting factors in (K_m∧K_n)^{∧p} and counting transpositions; injectivity on pn-skeleton assures the sign computation suffices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sq^0 is the identity and Sq^1 equals the Bockstein on generators
rubrics_metrics.description: Sq^0 acts as the identity on H^n for n>0. Sq^1 coincides with the mod 2 Bockstein β on the generator ω∈H^1(RP^2), and hence on its suspensions, so Sq^1 = β.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: compute ∇^*(λ(α)) for α a generator in low-dimensional examples (e.g., S^1) to show Sq^0(α)=α; use Cartan formula and suspension-commutation to extend to all n. For Sq^1 compare on ω in RP^2 and use suspension/naturality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commutation with suspension (stability property)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Sqi commutes with suspension σ: Sqi(σ(α)) = σ(Sqi(α)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument uses that σ(α)=ε⊗α where ε ∈ H^1(S^1) has Sq^0(ε)=ε and Sq^i(ε)=0 for i>0; then Cartan formula shows Sqi(σ(α))=ε⊗Sqi(α)=σ(Sqi(α)). This property yields stability/naturality and additivity for suspension-commuting operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adem relations for Steenrod squares
rubrics_metrics.description: The Adem relations hold for the Steenrod squares: specific linear relations among compositions Sq^i Sq^j reduce products to admissible monomials; the textbook gives a proof via symmetry of the Z_p×Z_p action and careful degree/dimension choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof technique: construct λ_2 using Z_p×Z_p-actions, compute ∇^*(λ_2(ι)) in two ways, analyze symmetry ϕ_{r s} = (−1)^{r s + p(p−1)n/2} ϕ_{s r} (for p=2 simplify to ϕ_{r s}=ϕ_{s r}), choose dimensions n of special dyadic form to isolate single terms, then use combinatorial/binomial coefficient identities to get the classical Adem formulas; suspend to extend to all dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vanishing pattern for θ_i when p is odd
rubrics_metrics.description: For odd prime p, θ_i = 0 unless i = 2k(p−1) or i = 2k(p−1)+1 (Lemma 4L.14).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument uses action of automorphisms of Z_p (multiplicative group Z_p^*) via a map ϕ which permutes factors and multiplies S^∞ coordinate; invariance forces the ω-exponent to have total ω_1/ω_2 count multiple of p−1, yielding the congruence conditions on i.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normalization constants a_n and multiplicative/sign relations
rubrics_metrics.description: The degree-preserving operation θ_0 : H^n → H^n is multiplication by some a_n∈Z_p, and the a_n satisfy multiplicative/sign relations: a_{m+n} = (−1)^{p(p−1)mn/2} a_m a_n and a_n = (−1)^{p(p−1)n(n−1)/4} a_n^{-1}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These relations come from the formula λ(α∪β) = (−1)^{p(p−1)mn/2} λ(α)λ(β) and induction; a_n is nonzero in Z_p so invertible. The normalization is fixed so that P^0 is the identity by dividing θ by a_n.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation a_1 = ± m! (with m=(p−1)/2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma 4L.15: a_1 = ± m! in Z_p where m = (p−1)/2, hence p = 2m+1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses geometry of the bundle and Thom class computation for the complementary bundle E→L_p built from the cyclic permutation linear map on R^p; decompose R^p into invariant subspaces V_0⊕…⊕V_m, compute Thom classes among subbundles E_j, and track pullbacks to conclude the factor ±m! appears in ∇^*(λ(α)). This ensures a_1 is nonzero modulo p.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Steenrod powers P^i for odd p
rubrics_metrics.description: For α∈H^n, define P^i(α) = (−1)^i a_n^{-1} θ_{2i(p−1)}(α), where a_n is the invertible normalization constant, so that P^0 is the identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The factor a_n^{-1} guarantees P^0 = id; the (−1)^i factor is chosen to make P^i(α)=α^p when |α|=2i. Prior lemmas (vanishing pattern, a_1 value, number-theoretic congruences) are used to verify normalization and axioms (including P^0=1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Number-theoretic congruence used for normalization
rubrics_metrics.description: The factorial congruence ((p−1)/2)!^2 ≡ (−1)^{(p+1)/2} (mod p) is used to check normalization a_n and the property a_{2i} = (−1)^i for certain indices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument: product of ±1,±2,...,±(p−1)/2 equals the unique element of order 2 in Z_p^*, namely −1; combine with prior multiplicative relations on a_n to deduce required parity/congruence.
